title: The Mystery Bruise
style: film noir jazz, 88 BPM, walking upright bass, brushed snare, smoky tenor saxophone, vibraphone, deadpan male storyteller vocal, detective comedy delivery, dimly lit lounge atmosphere
lyrics:
[Intro — film noir jazz, brushed snare, walking bass, detective tone]
A bruise. Yellow at the edges, purple in the middle. Left thigh.
And a witness — myself — who saw nothing.

[Verse 1 — male, deadpan investigator]
The body was discovered at seven oh three
In the bathroom mirror, by the man holding the keys to me
Approximately the size of a lemon, slightly oblong
The victim and the suspect have been together all along

[Pre-Chorus]
Did I bump the corner of the bedside drawer?
Did I roll into the dog at four?
Did I battle the laundry hamper at three?
Did I slay a coffee table I didn't see?

[Chorus]
The mystery bruise! The mystery bruise!
A purple yellow story without a clue
The mystery bruise! The mystery bruise!
The body has receipts but the mind does too
The mystery bruise!

[Verse 2 — male]
I was the only person in the room when it happened
I was awake the whole time, allegedly the captain
Yet here is the bruise like a postcard from a stranger
Saying greetings from your shin, signed your endangered ranger

[Pre-Chorus]
Was it the doorframe? Was it the chair?
Was it the cat in the dark on the stair?
Was it a dream where I jumped from a tree?
Did my own body sleepwalk and assault me?

[Chorus]
The mystery bruise! The mystery bruise!
A purple yellow story without a clue
The mystery bruise! The mystery bruise!
The body has receipts but the mind does too
The mystery bruise!

[Bridge — sax solo, then spoken]
[detective] Did you do this to yourself?
[me] I plead the fifth.
[detective] You are the fifth.
[me] …I rest my case.

[Outro]
The mystery bruise!
Forty years old and getting injured by furniture
The mystery bruise!
